title: Biden’s Radical Option to End the Debt Fight

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即便是在黑胶唱片时代，我还在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔瓦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I just finished, I thought, a productive meeting with the congressional leadership about the path forward to make sure America does not default.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚结束了与国会领导层关于未来路径的会议，我认为会议很有成效，旨在确保美国不会违约。

sentences.en: In a high-stakes showdown this week, President Biden and the leaders of Congress met face-to-face in an attempt to avoid the U.S.
sentences.zh: 本周，在一场高风险的对峙中，拜登总统与国会领导人面对面会谈，试图避免美国

sentences.en: defaulting on its debt for the first time in history.
sentences.zh: 历史上首次出现债务违约。

sentences.en: America is not a deadbeat nation.
sentences.zh: 美国不是一个赖账的国家。

sentences.en: We pay our bills and avoiding default is a basic duty of the United States Congress.
sentences.zh: 我们支付账单，避免违约是美国国会的基本职责。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Jim Tangersley on how close the country now is to that financial calamity and the radical step Biden might take to prevent it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事吉姆·坦格斯利将讲述这个国家距离金融灾难有多近，以及拜登为防止灾难可能采取的激进措施。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 12th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月12日，星期五。

sentences.en: So, Jim, the federal government, as we all know, is in this rather frantic process of trying to avoid the nation defaulting on its debts.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，众所周知，联邦政府正处于一种相当狂乱的过程中，试图避免国家债务违约。

sentences.en: And we talked on the show last week about how that poses this really big challenge for the Speaker of the House, Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 我们在上周的节目中讨论过，这对众议院议长凯文·麦卡锡来说是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: But, of course, it also poses a really big challenge for President Biden.
sentences.zh: 当然，这对拜登总统来说也是一个巨大的挑战。

sentences.en: So, walk me through the debt limit dilemma from his point of view.
sentences.zh: 那么，请从他的角度为我梳理一下债务上限的困境。

sentences.en: What does this look like if you're Biden?
sentences.zh: 如果你是拜登，这看起来会是什么样？

sentences.en: So, on Tuesday, President Biden welcomed Speaker McCarthy and other congressional leaders from both parties to the White House.
sentences.zh: 周二，拜登总统在白宫欢迎了麦卡锡议长和其他两党的国会领导人。

sentences.en: And for all intents and purposes, this really was a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 从各方面来看，这确实是一场谈判。

sentences.en: The timing of these talks has everything to do with what's going on right now with the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 这些会谈的时机与债务上限目前的情况密切相关。

sentences.en: From the president's perspective, what's happening here is that Republicans are holding the nation hostage.
sentences.zh: 从总统的角度来看，共和党人正在绑架这个国家。

sentences.en: They're basically saying we might let the government default on debt catastrophically for the economy unless President Biden agrees to a whole bunch of cuts in federal spending.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在说，除非拜登总统同意削减大量联邦支出，否则我们可能会让政府违约，从而对经济造成灾难性后果。

sentences.en: The president has no intention of agreeing to the wide scope of cuts Republicans have talked about.
sentences.zh: 总统无意同意共和党人所谈论的大规模削减开支。

sentences.en: And he's really opposed to the idea that he should have to negotiate at all over what he basically views as Congress's responsibility to raise the limit to pay the bills Congress has already authorized.
sentences.zh: 他非常反对自己必须就他认为属于国会责任的事情进行谈判，即提高上限以支付国会已经授权的账单。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: Now, from a Republican's perspective, Biden's being unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 现在，从共和党的角度来看，拜登是不合理的。

sentences.en: They have passed a bill that raises the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 他们已经通过了一项提高债务上限的法案。

sentences.en: And even though it comes with strings that he doesn't like attached to it, that should be reason for him to sit down and say, OK, what can we agree on here?
sentences.zh: 即使该法案附带了他不喜欢的条件，那也应该成为他坐下来谈谈“我们能达成什么共识”的理由，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, all of that in mind, the parties come to the White House on Tuesday afternoon, they sit down,
sentences.zh: 所以，带着这些想法，双方在周二下午来到白宫坐下，

sentences.en: and there's real urgency behind the talks because we are barreling toward what is known as the X date.
sentences.zh: 会谈背后有着真正的紧迫感，因为我们正全速冲向所谓的“X日”。

sentences.en: It's the time when the Treasury Department is going to run out of its ability to pay all of the government's bills on time.
sentences.zh: 那是财政部将耗尽按时支付政府所有账单能力的时间点。

sentences.en: And Treasury officials have recently estimated that date could hit as soon as June 1St.
sentences.zh: 财政部官员最近估计，这一日期最早可能在6月1日到来。

sentences.en: Which is really soon.
sentences.zh: 那真的很快了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's basically no time at all.
sentences.zh: 是的，基本上没剩多少时间了。

sentences.en: But so far in their talks, the president and Republicans of Congress have made almost no progress in finding common ground.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，总统和国会共和党人在寻找共同点方面几乎没有取得任何进展。

sentences.en: They're sort of stuck in a game of chicken with each one kind of pointing the finger at the other and expecting that they will blink first,
sentences.zh: 他们陷入了一种胆小鬼博弈，每个人都指责对方，并期待对方先退缩，

sentences.en: give in to the other side's demands to avoid a default.
sentences.zh: 为了避免违约而屈服于对方的要求。

sentences.en: And that's a really perilous position for the economy and the country right now.
sentences.zh: 这对目前的经济和国家来说是一个非常危险的处境。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, basically, up until this point, things have been kind of at a stalemate between the two sides.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上到目前为止，双方一直处于僵局。

sentences.en: What can Biden do about it?
sentences.zh: 拜登能做些什么呢？

sentences.en: Well,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: the first is that he could put an end to that game of chicken and attempt to negotiate a deal with Speaker McCarthy that would be acceptable to both the speaker and to the president.
sentences.zh: 首先，他可以结束那场胆小鬼博弈，尝试与麦卡锡议长达成一项双方都能接受的协议。

sentences.en: And probably what that would mean is some sort of agreement built around some kind of limits on federal discretionary spending over a period of a few years.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着达成某种协议，在几年内对联邦可自由支配支出设定某种限制。

sentences.en: There's a reason in particular that White House officials talk about spending limits as a possible anchor of a deal, and it's because they don't expect to increase spending anyway,
sentences.zh: 白宫官员谈论支出限制作为协议的锚点是有特定原因的，因为他们本来就不指望增加支出，

sentences.en: so long as Republicans control the House.
sentences.zh: 只要共和党控制众议院的话。

sentences.en: So, if they just effectively agree to put into writing what they expect to happen already, well, the president might go for that.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果他们只是有效地同意将他们预期会发生的事情写下来，那么总统可能会接受。

sentences.en: In addition to that, though, the president signaled on Tuesday that he might be willing to cut some spending in a way that Republicans have been pushing for for a while.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，总统周二还暗示，他可能愿意以共和党人一直推动的方式削减一些开支。

sentences.en: Specifically, he would be open to canceling some of the money that was included in the stimulus bill he signed in 2021 but hasn't been spent yet.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他愿意取消他在2021年签署的刺激法案中包含但尚未支出的部分资金。

sentences.en: Now, Republicans estimate that cancellation would save $50 to $70 billion, but that's a really small slice of their total proposal to raise the debt limit and cut spending,
sentences.zh: 共和党人估计，这种取消将节省500亿到700亿美元，但这在他们提高债务上限和削减开支的总提案中只占很小一部分，

sentences.en: which actually sums up to nearly $5 trillion.
sentences.zh: 该提案总额实际上接近5万亿美元。

sentences.en: Okay, so in this option, Biden would say, look, I'll agree to a more moderate set of spending cuts, and in return, Speaker McCarthy, you'll go ahead and raise the debt limit,
sentences.zh: 好的，所以在这个选项中，拜登会说，看，我同意采取一套更温和的削减开支方案，作为回报，麦卡锡议长，你继续提高债务上限，

sentences.en: no strings attached.
sentences.zh: 不附带任何条件。

sentences.en: That's certainly one of the things that a lot of folks around Washington expect could be an outcome of these discussions.
sentences.zh: 这当然是华盛顿许多人预期可能成为这些讨论结果的事情之一。

sentences.en: But it's not clear that would work.
sentences.zh: 但目前还不清楚这是否行得通。

sentences.en: Speaker McCarthy would have to sell that compromise to Republicans in the House, and there are a lot of them who have really been agitating for much,
sentences.zh: 麦卡锡议长必须向众议院的共和党人推销这种妥协，他们中有许多人一直在极力要求比总统达成的任何协议都要深得多、

sentences.en: much deeper cuts than any kind of deal with the president would entail, and who could very likely refuse to vote for it.
sentences.zh: 多得多的削减，而且他们很可能会拒绝投票支持。

sentences.en: Right, so big potential pitfalls to that one.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以这个方案有很大的潜在陷阱。

sentences.en: So what's the next option then?
sentences.zh: 那么下一个选项是什么？

sentences.en: Well, if the president decides that it's just not fruitful to talk to the speaker, he could try to go around Kevin McCarthy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果总统认为与议长谈话没有成效，他可以尝试绕过凯文·麦卡锡。

sentences.en: He could try to cut a deal with just enough Republican votes to join with Democrats in the House and the Senate to raise the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 他可以尝试争取足够多的共和党票数，与众议院和参议院的民主党人联合起来提高债务上限。

sentences.en: That would require doing something to bring probably five Republicans in the House on board and close to 10 Republicans in the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这需要采取行动，争取众议院大约5名共和党人和参议院近10名共和党人的支持。

sentences.en: They'd have to probably use this legislative maneuver called a discharge petition.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不得不使用一种名为“解除请愿”的立法手段。

sentences.en: Oh, boy.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's a way to bring a bill to the floor for a vote in the House, even if the Speaker of the House doesn't want it there.
sentences.zh: 这是一种即使众议院议长不希望法案进入表决程序，也能将其提交众议院投票的方法。

sentences.en: So, theoretically,
sentences.zh: 所以，理论上，

sentences.en: they could do this arcane process to bring up a bill that they have a small number of Republicans agreeing on to pass a debt limit increase with mostly Democratic votes.
sentences.zh: 他们可以通过这个深奥的过程，提出一项有少数共和党人同意的法案，以主要依靠民主党票数通过债务上限的提高。

sentences.en: It's really tricky.
sentences.zh: 这真的很棘手。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of time legislatively.
sentences.zh: 在立法上需要花费很多时间。

sentences.en: It takes a lot of political capital,
sentences.zh: 需要消耗大量的政治资本，

sentences.en: and there's no indication that the sort of discussions are going on with Republicans or that there's even an appetite among Republicans to make this happen.
sentences.zh: 而且没有任何迹象表明共和党内部正在进行此类讨论，甚至没有共和党人愿意促成此事。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So, these options don't look particularly easy.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些选项看起来都不容易。

sentences.en: Either get Republicans to agree to weigh less than what they're asking for or convince enough Republicans to turn their back on their party.
sentences.zh: 要么让共和党人同意远低于他们要求的条件，要么说服足够的共和党人背弃他们的政党。

sentences.en: Well, yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的。

sentences.en: None of the legislative options are perfect.
sentences.zh: 没有任何立法选项是完美的。

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And it is what's giving a lot of heartburn to people who watch Congress right now is that they're having a hard time seeing how it would work.
sentences.zh: 这让现在关注国会的人感到非常揪心，因为他们很难看出这该如何运作。

sentences.en: But there is another option that the administration is weighing.
sentences.zh: 但政府正在权衡另一个选项。

sentences.en: It's actually something that they've been talking about for months that is still on the table today and would be, I wouldn't call it a nuclear option, but a really big,
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是他们几个月来一直在讨论的事情，今天仍然摆在桌面上，而且，我不会称之为“核选项”，但这是一个非常大、

sentences.en: bold risk that the president could take to try to end this debt limit fight by himself.
sentences.zh: 大胆的风险，总统可以独自采取行动来试图结束这场债务上限之争。

sentences.en: And what's that option?
sentences.zh: 那个选项是什么？

sentences.en: The president could decide to ignore Congress and ignore the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 总统可以决定无视国会，无视债务上限。

sentences.en: He could follow a theory of the Constitution that is effectively a constitutional challenge to the existence of the debt limit itself.
sentences.zh: 他可以遵循一种宪法理论，实际上是对债务上限本身的存在提出宪法挑战。

sentences.en: It's rooted in the 14th Amendment to the Constitution, which effectively says the government has to pay its debts.
sentences.zh: 它植根于宪法第14修正案，该修正案实际上规定政府必须偿还债务。

sentences.en: It can't just not pay.
sentences.zh: 它不能仅仅是不支付。

sentences.en: But the 14th Amendment, like the 14th Amendment?
sentences.zh: 但是第14修正案，是指那个第14修正案吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那个第14修正案。

sentences.en: I mean, that was the amendment that was passed after the Civil War, and it was about slavery, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是内战后通过的修正案，是关于奴隶制的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what does it have to do with the nation's debt?
sentences.zh: 那它和国家的债务有什么关系？

sentences.en: OK, it's wonky, but bear with me here.
sentences.zh: 好的，这很深奥，但请听我解释。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: As you just said,
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才所说，

sentences.en: the 14th Amendment is adopted right after the Civil War at a time when lawmakers are setting out the terms under which the states that had seceded to join the Confederacy would be allowed to come back into the Union.
sentences.zh: 第14修正案是在内战后通过的，当时立法者正在制定条款，规定那些脱离联邦加入邦联的州在什么条件下可以被允许重新加入联邦。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It does a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 它做了很多事情。

sentences.en: It granted citizenship to former slaves, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，它赋予了前奴隶公民身份。

sentences.en: But it also includes a section, Section 4, if you're scoring at home, that says the validity of the public debt of the United States shall not be questioned.
sentences.zh: 但它也包含了一个条款，即第4款——如果你在家里做笔记的话——它规定美国公共债务的有效性不容置疑。

sentences.en: And there's sort of a quirky reason why they did that.
sentences.zh: 他们这样做有一个奇特的原因。

sentences.en: It was about sort of the fears of Southern states regaining political power in a new Congress.
sentences.zh: 这与担心南方各州在新国会中重新获得政治权力有关。

sentences.en: You know, the United States had borrowed money to finance the Union Army in the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 你知道，美国曾借钱资助内战中的联邦军队。

sentences.en: And there was a worry that if Southern senators and representatives controlled Congress, they could just decide, oh,
sentences.zh: 当时人们担心，如果南方参议员和众议员控制了国会，他们可能会决定，哦，

sentences.en: we're not going to pay the people we borrowed money from for a war, you know, against our own states.
sentences.zh: 我们不打算偿还那些我们借钱打仗的人，你知道，那是针对我们自己州的战争。

sentences.en: Oh, interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，有意思。

sentences.en: So they wanted to make sure that in the Constitution it said, nope, you have to pay all the debts.
sentences.zh: 所以他们想确保宪法里写着，不，你必须偿还所有债务。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So they were coming back in, having political representation in Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以他们回来后，在国会拥有了政治代表权。

sentences.en: And the idea was, no, you have to accept and take on all of the debts.
sentences.zh: 当时的想法是，不，你必须接受并承担所有的债务。

sentences.en: You can't back out of them.
sentences.zh: 你不能背弃它们。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So under that theory, a president like President Biden could decide that the Constitution trumps the law and that in this case,
sentences.zh: 所以根据这个理论，像拜登总统这样的总统可以决定宪法高于法律，在这种情况下，

sentences.en: it requires the government to keep issuing new debt to pay off its old debts, no matter what the debt limit says.
sentences.zh: 它要求政府继续发行新债来偿还旧债，无论债务上限怎么说。

sentences.en: So this clause has been around for a long time, right, since the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 所以这个条款已经存在很长时间了，对吧，从19世纪开始。

sentences.en: Why haven't other presidents who faced this problem used it?
sentences.zh: 为什么其他面临这个问题的总统没有使用它？

sentences.en: It has been around.
sentences.zh: 它确实存在。

sentences.en: And this is not the first time it's come up.
sentences.zh: 而且这也不是第一次被提出来。

sentences.en: It was raised in like a law review article at the end of the 90s.
sentences.zh: 它在90年代末的一篇法律评论文章中被提到过。

sentences.en: But it really kind of entered the conversation from obscurity in 2011.
sentences.zh: 但它真正从默默无闻进入大众视野是在2011年。

sentences.en: After seven plus months of scathing political attacks, countless meetings between the president and lawmakers, there is still no debt ceiling deal.
sentences.zh: 在经历了七个多月的激烈政治攻击、总统与立法者之间无数次会议后，仍然没有达成债务上限协议。

sentences.en: When President Obama had that debt ceiling fight with Republicans in the House.
sentences.zh: 当时奥巴马总统与众议院共和党人进行了那场债务上限之争。

sentences.en: Some top tier Democrats have said, hmm, the 14th Amendment, that might work for us.
sentences.zh: 一些顶级民主党人说，嗯，第14修正案，这对我们可能有效。

sentences.en: At the time, there was a lot of buzz about it.
sentences.zh: 当时，关于它的讨论非常多。

sentences.en: I'm hearing people talk a little bit more about the feasibility of this 14th Amendment option.
sentences.zh: 我听到人们更多地谈论这个第14修正案选项的可行性。

sentences.en: Even former President Bill Clinton said that he would have invoked the amendment if he was still president.
sentences.zh: 甚至前总统比尔·克林顿也表示，如果他还是总统，他会援引该修正案。

sentences.en: There's a strong argument for what Bill Clinton has argued.
sentences.zh: 比尔·克林顿所主张的观点有很强的论据支持。

sentences.en: But inside the Obama White House.
sentences.zh: 但在奥巴马白宫内部。

sentences.en: I have talked to my lawyers.
sentences.zh: 我和我的律师谈过。

sentences.en: They don't, they do not, they are not persuaded that that is a winning argument.
sentences.zh: 他们不，他们不，他们不相信这是一个有说服力的论点。

sentences.en: They never really seriously consider this.
sentences.zh: 他们从未真正认真考虑过这一点。

sentences.en: And why didn't they consider it seriously?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么没有认真考虑呢？

sentences.en: Well, first off, it's not clear cut in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，它在宪法中并不明确。

sentences.en: The Constitution also says that taxing and spending resides with Congress.
sentences.zh: 宪法也规定征税和支出权属于国会。

sentences.en: So it's a theory and it's a theory that has some scholarship behind it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个理论，而且是一个有一定学术支持的理论。

sentences.en: But it's not a cut and dry, everyone agrees on it interpretation of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 但它并不是一个每个人都同意的、简单明了的宪法解释。

sentences.en: But beyond that, there were other considerations driving the Obama team when they didn't consider this and that are giving the Biden team pause now.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，奥巴马团队在没有考虑这一点时还有其他考量，而这些考量现在也让拜登团队犹豫不决。

sentences.en: And the biggest one is this.
sentences.zh: 最重要的一点是这个。

sentences.en: Even if a president were to believe that this is constitutionally the right thing to do and take this leap, that leap would bring some really profound consequences.
sentences.zh: 即使总统认为从宪法角度来看这是正确的做法并采取这一行动，这一举动也会带来一些非常深远的后果。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝成立175周年，致力于帮助您了解世界，充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享特别优惠，请访问 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: Okay, so Jim, walk me through what the consequences would be if the Biden administration actually decides to go for this thing, the 14th Amendment strategy.
sentences.zh: 好的，吉姆，请给我梳理一下，如果拜登政府真的决定采取这一举措，即第14修正案策略，会有什么后果？

sentences.en: Well, first off, we don't know exactly what would happen,
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我们并不确切知道会发生什么，

sentences.en: but I don't think it would be that the president would step outside the White House one day and run out and scream into the void, I invoke the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 但我认为总统不会有一天走出白宫，冲着虚空大喊：“我援引第14修正案。”

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: But, I mean, unlikely.
sentences.zh: 我是说，不太可能。

sentences.en: Possible.
sentences.zh: 有可能。

sentences.en: Good television.
sentences.zh: 电视效果不错。

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我不这么认为。

sentences.en: But as the June 1st deadline approaches, the government, you know, runs out of the ability to pay its bills.
sentences.zh: 但随着6月1日最后期限的临近，政府，你知道，将失去支付账单的能力。

sentences.en: So the president will essentially say, okay, I'm going to call the Treasury Secretary and tell her that we are invoking the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以总统基本上会说，好吧，我要给财政部长打电话，告诉她我们要援引第14修正案。

sentences.en: And so we need to have another round of raising money to pay our debts.
sentences.zh: 我们需要进行新一轮的融资来偿还债务。

sentences.en: Like Janet Yellen, the Treasury Secretary, can just do that.
sentences.zh: 就像财政部长珍妮特·耶伦可以直接那样做一样。

sentences.en: Well, her department holds what's called a Treasury auction.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她的部门会举行所谓的国债拍卖。

sentences.en: Happens all the time,
sentences.zh: 这经常发生，

sentences.en: and it's when the government goes out and sells new bonds to lenders who are essentially giving the government money now in exchange for the government giving them some more money later on down the road.
sentences.zh: 就是政府向贷款人出售新债券，贷款人本质上是现在给政府钱，以换取政府在未来某个时候给他们更多的钱。

sentences.en: So Biden calling up Yellen says, just do another Treasury auction.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登打电话给耶伦说，再做一次国债拍卖吧。

sentences.en: We do them every week.
sentences.zh: 我们每周都做。

sentences.en: Do one this week.
sentences.zh: 这周做一次。

sentences.en: Like, that sounds okay, right?
sentences.zh: 这听起来没问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, where's the problem there?
sentences.zh: 问题出在哪里呢？

sentences.en: Well, the problem is probably in the auction itself, and it's specifically with the buyers of the government bonds.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题可能出在拍卖本身，具体来说是政府债券的买家。

sentences.en: They, for good reason, might not be so sure that this debt they would be borrowing is actually going to pay off down the road.
sentences.zh: 他们有充分的理由怀疑，他们借出的这笔债未来是否真的能偿还。

sentences.en: If there's a constitutional question about whether the government will actually be allowed to issue these bonds, well, then maybe you're buying something that's worthless.
sentences.zh: 如果关于政府是否真的被允许发行这些债券存在宪法争议，那么你买的可能就是废纸。

sentences.en: So those buyers in the Treasury auction are going to do what buyers in auctions do all the time when they're buying a riskier asset,
sentences.zh: 所以国债拍卖中的买家会做买家在购买高风险资产时常做的事，

sentences.en: which is they're going to pay less money for it.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们会为此支付更少的钱。

sentences.en: And what effectively does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着什么？

sentences.en: Effectively what it means is that the government is going to have to pay a much higher interest rate to borrow money in the short term.
sentences.zh: 实际上这意味着政府将不得不支付更高的利率来短期借款。

sentences.en: It's kind of like taking out a payday loan with a really high rate.
sentences.zh: 这有点像借了一笔利率极高的发薪日贷款。

sentences.en: But would the financial fallout here be worse than if the government just defaulted on its debt altogether?
sentences.zh: 但这里的金融后果会比政府直接债务违约更严重吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不会。

sentences.en: I mean, that is a big part of the consideration here.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是这里考量的一个重要部分。

sentences.en: I mean, this would be chaos.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这会是一场混乱。

sentences.en: An actual default on the debt could be crippling chaos.
sentences.zh: 真正的债务违约可能会造成毁灭性的混乱。

sentences.en: If the debt limit is hit and we truly breach the X state, the markets are going to go nuts no matter what Biden does and not just Treasury markets.
sentences.zh: 如果触及债务上限，我们真的突破了X日期，无论拜登做什么，市场都会发疯，而且不仅仅是国债市场。

sentences.en: But in this case, what's going to happen is the government is going to at least keep that money flowing into the economy,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，政府至少会保持资金流入经济，

sentences.en: which will be less of a disruption than if it just stopped paying people.
sentences.zh: 这比直接停止向人们付款造成的破坏要小。

sentences.en: And the tradeoff is it's going to be paying a really high interest rate to borrow that money to keep flowing.
sentences.zh: 代价是它将不得不支付极高的利率来借钱以维持资金流动。

sentences.en: So these are the financial perils.
sentences.zh: 所以这些就是金融风险。

sentences.en: But I mean, there must be some pretty serious legal consequences here, too, right?
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这里肯定也有相当严重的法律后果，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Biden is essentially circumventing Congress.
sentences.zh: 我是说，拜登基本上是在绕过国会。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, it is basically a guarantee that someone would challenge this in court if Biden did it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果拜登这样做，几乎可以肯定有人会在法庭上挑战这一举措。

sentences.en: And what would that look like?
sentences.zh: 那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Well, there's a real chance that some lower court somewhere in the country would decide that, in fact, the government can't do this,
sentences.zh: 嗯，很有可能全国某个下级法院会裁定，事实上，政府不能这样做，

sentences.en: that the Constitution does not say what Biden is saying.
sentences.zh: 宪法并没有说拜登所说的那样。

sentences.en: And that the Constitution vests power for taxing and spending only with Congress and the Biden administration would appeal.
sentences.zh: 而且宪法将征税和支出的权力仅授予国会，拜登政府会提出上诉。

sentences.en: And it would very likely end up at the United States Supreme Court because, you know, that is how these big fights seem to end up these days.
sentences.zh: 而且它很可能会最终上诉到美国最高法院，因为，你知道，这些重大争端如今似乎都是这样收场的。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: So, OK, it gets the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，它到了最高法院。

sentences.en: Then what?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: Well, Supreme Court could decide any number of things.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最高法院可以做出任何决定。

sentences.en: On the one hand, they could decide that the plaintiff is correct, that the government cannot issue any more debt.
sentences.zh: 一方面，他们可以裁定原告是正确的，政府不能再发行任何债务。

sentences.en: And it might say that debt is invalid that was just issued in the Treasury auction or that the government has to give the buyers their money back.
sentences.zh: 它可能会说刚刚在国债拍卖中发行的债务是无效的，或者政府必须把钱退还给买家。

sentences.en: So that would then cause the default that the administration had been trying to avoid.
sentences.zh: 那么这就会导致政府一直试图避免的违约。

sentences.en: All the government spending would come to a halt.
sentences.zh: 所有的政府支出都会停止。

sentences.en: Pretty dire economic situation.
sentences.zh: 相当可怕的经济状况。

sentences.en: And presumably what those bond buyers were worried about, right?
sentences.zh: 大概就是那些债券买家所担心的，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the Supreme Court could side with Biden.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，最高法院可能站在拜登一边。

sentences.en: And that could happen in actually a couple of different ways.
sentences.zh: 这实际上可以通过几种不同的方式发生。

sentences.en: For one, it could decide that no one has standing to sue to challenge Biden's move because you need to show harm in order to be a plaintiff in a case like this.
sentences.zh: 首先，它可以裁定没有人有资格起诉挑战拜登的举动，因为要成为此类案件的原告，你需要证明受到了损害。

sentences.en: And the court could decide that, well, no one is harmed by the government continuing to issue debt.
sentences.zh: 法院可以裁定，嗯，政府继续发行债务并没有损害任何人。

sentences.en: The second thing it could do, of course, is just agree with this interpretation of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 当然，它能做的第二件事就是同意这种对宪法的解释。

sentences.en: It could say the president is correct, the 14th Amendment overrides the law, and the government must keep paying its debts.
sentences.zh: 它可以说总统是正确的，第14修正案凌驾于法律之上，政府必须继续偿还债务。

sentences.en: In either of those scenarios, it would effectively be agreeing with Biden that the debt limit is unconstitutional and basically strike it down.
sentences.zh: 在任何一种情况下，它实际上都会同意拜登的观点，即债务上限是违宪的，并基本上将其废除。

sentences.en: So in that scenario, I mean, if the administration did move forward with this constitutional strategy and it worked, as you're describing there,
sentences.zh: 那么在这种情况下，我是说，如果政府真的推进了这个宪法策略并且成功了，正如你所描述的那样，

sentences.en: it would mean the end of these debt limit fights altogether, right?
sentences.zh: 这意味着这些债务上限的争斗将彻底结束，对吧？

sentences.en: Which would seem to be a bit of a political earthquake.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一场政治地震。

sentences.en: It would be.
sentences.zh: 确实会是。

sentences.en: It would be a political earthquake.
sentences.zh: 那将是一场政治地震。

sentences.en: It's certainly something that a lot of Democrats and progressives who have pushed this interpretation of the Constitution for a long time would love to see.
sentences.zh: 这当然是许多长期以来一直推动这种宪法解释的民主党人和进步派人士乐于看到的。

sentences.en: They would call it an end to the Republican hostage taking over the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 他们会称之为共和党人以债务上限为要挟的终结。

sentences.en: Short term, however, it would be a really big mess for the operations of this Congress and this government or this president.
sentences.zh: 然而，短期内，这对本届国会和本届政府或这位总统的运作来说将是一个巨大的烂摊子。

sentences.en: Describe that mess.
sentences.zh: 描述一下那个烂摊子。

sentences.en: Well, very bluntly put, it would make Republicans really angry and they could retaliate in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，直白地说，这会让共和党人非常愤怒，他们可以通过多种方式进行报复。

sentences.en: One of the easiest ways they could retaliate is by deciding, hey,
sentences.zh: 他们可以报复的最简单方法之一就是决定，嘿，

sentences.en: the money that funds all of the government services that people know and use runs out at the end of September and we're just not going to pass a bill appropriating any more money until Biden,
sentences.zh: 资助人们所知和使用的所有政府服务的资金在9月底用完，我们就是不通过任何拨款法案，直到拜登，

sentences.en: you know, reverses course on the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在债务上限问题上改变方针。

sentences.en: So essentially, even if Janet Yellen is out there raising money, having these debt auctions,
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，即使珍妮特·耶伦在外面筹集资金，进行这些债务拍卖，

sentences.en: there are ways that Congress can still throw some pretty serious hurdles in the way of the government's finances.
sentences.zh: 国会仍然可以通过一些相当严重的障碍来阻碍政府的财政。

sentences.en: Yeah, Congress has to appropriate the money to run basic government operations.
sentences.zh: 是的，国会必须拨款来维持基本的政府运作。

sentences.en: Now, everything from the military to the education department to the national parks,
sentences.zh: 现在，从军队到教育部再到国家公园，一切都是如此，

sentences.en: and they could just decide in protest not to do that for a while or indefinitely until the president comes to the table and meets their demands.
sentences.zh: 他们可以仅仅为了抗议而决定暂时或无限期地不这样做，直到总统坐到谈判桌前满足他们的要求。

sentences.en: So even if Biden does this, you know, and it goes OK, or at the very least, it doesn't blow up completely, it's still pretty politically risky for him.
sentences.zh: 所以即使拜登这样做了，你知道，而且进展顺利，或者至少没有完全搞砸，对他来说在政治上仍然是相当冒险的。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a political consideration that has been discussed inside the administration, and that risk extends well beyond Congress.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是政府内部讨论过的一个政治考量，这种风险远远超出了国会。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's very fair to say that we have no idea what public opinion would be about this.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为可以公平地说，我们完全不知道公众对此会有什么看法。

sentences.en: It's certainly not something that's been debated in the open.
sentences.zh: 这当然不是在公开场合辩论过的事情。

sentences.en: It hasn't been aired in campaign commercials.
sentences.zh: 它没有在竞选广告中播出过。

sentences.en: You know, the president is just starting to run for re-election, and he'd be taking a risk here,
sentences.zh: 你知道，总统才刚刚开始竞选连任，他在这里要冒一个险，

sentences.en: hoping that voters would reward him for acting decisively to keep the nation from defaulting, but worrying that voters might get angry about it.
sentences.zh: 希望选民能因为他果断行动防止国家违约而奖励他，但又担心选民可能会因此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And often when voters are angry, they blame the president.
sentences.zh: 而且通常当选民愤怒时，他们会责怪总统。

sentences.en: So that's a risk for him as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这对他也构成风险。

sentences.en: So, Jim, big picture here, how likely is it that this 14th Amendment strategy actually gets used by the Biden administration, I mean, given these risks you're laying out?
sentences.zh: 那么，吉姆，从大局来看，拜登政府真正使用这种第14修正案策略的可能性有多大？我是说，考虑到你列出的这些风险？

sentences.en: Well, something really interesting on this happened on Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 嗯，周二发生了一件非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: After his meeting with congressional leaders,
sentences.zh: 在他与国会领导人会面后，

sentences.en: This nation is never to fall on its debt.
sentences.zh: 这个国家绝不能在债务上违约。

sentences.en: It never will.
sentences.zh: 永远不会。

sentences.en: President Biden gave a statement.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统发表了一份声明。

sentences.en: Thank you, and I'll take your questions.
sentences.zh: 谢谢，我会回答你们的问题。

sentences.en: And then took questions from reporters.
sentences.zh: 然后接受了记者的提问。

sentences.en: If you do, you said you're certain you're not going to.
sentences.zh: 如果你这样做，你说你确定你不会。

sentences.en: And he was asked if he would consider invoking the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 有人问他是否会考虑援引第14修正案。

sentences.en: Well, the question, I have been considering the 14th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个问题，我一直在考虑第14修正案。

sentences.en: He said he was looking at it.
sentences.zh: 他说他正在研究它。

sentences.en: But the problem is it would have to be litigated.
sentences.zh: 但问题是它必须经过诉讼。

sentences.en: He mentioned the legal reasons why it might not be a great idea, but he explicitly kept it on the table.
sentences.zh: 他提到了为什么这可能不是一个好主意的法律原因，但他明确表示保留这一选项。

sentences.en: There have been discussions about whether or not the 14th Amendment can be invoked.
sentences.zh: 关于是否可以援引第14修正案，已经有过讨论。

sentences.en: Is that the most likely?
sentences.zh: 这是最可能的吗？

sentences.en: I think that's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很重要。

sentences.en: I think it certainly makes it much more likely that it could happen than people thought weeks ago when the president is refusing to rule it out in public in the midst of these talks with Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我认为这当然使得它发生的可能性比几周前人们认为的要大得多，因为总统在与共和党人进行这些会谈时拒绝在公开场合排除这一选项。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Now, with all that said, I think there's still a decent chance that whether it's through negotiation or a steering contest or whatever,
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，我认为无论是通过谈判还是僵持，或者其他什么方式，

sentences.en: the president and Congress end with an agreement to raise the debt limit before we hit the X date.
sentences.zh: 总统和国会最终达成协议在X日期之前提高债务上限的可能性仍然很大。

sentences.en: That could mean kicking the can down the road just a little bit, a month or two to give them more time to talk about the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着把问题往后推一点，一两个月，给他们更多的时间来讨论债务上限。

sentences.en: And there's always this possibility that financial markets will freak out right before a possible default and that that could spur Congress to act.
sentences.zh: 而且总是有可能金融市场会在可能违约之前惊慌失措，这可能会促使国会采取行动。

sentences.en: But regardless of whether Biden actually pulls the trigger on this 14th Amendment idea,
sentences.zh: 但无论拜登是否真的扣动了第14修正案这个想法的扳机，

sentences.en: isn't the fact that it's become such a point of conversation kind of meaningful in and of itself?
sentences.zh: 它成为这样一个谈话焦点，这本身难道不就很有意义吗？

sentences.en: Like we've gotten to this point that this option is on the table.
sentences.zh: 就像我们已经到了这个地步，这个选项被摆在了桌面上。

sentences.en: I mean, what does that tell us about where we are right now as a country, as a political system?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这告诉我们作为国家、作为政治体系，我们现在处于什么位置？

sentences.en: I actually had an interview this week with someone who has been around Washington for a long time and was talking to me on background about this crisis.
sentences.zh: 我本周确实采访了一个在华盛顿待了很长时间的人，他私下里和我谈论了这场危机。

sentences.en: And what he said was, I think, very resonant to this question, which was no one trusts each other in Washington like they used to.
sentences.zh: 我认为他所说的话对这个问题非常有共鸣，那就是在华盛顿，没有人像过去那样信任彼此了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Inside the Biden administration, they do not trust that Republicans are actually going to raise the debt limit in time in the same way that the Obama administration trusted that.
sentences.zh: 在拜登政府内部，他们不相信共和党人会像奥巴马政府所信任的那样及时提高债务上限。

sentences.en: And Republicans don't trust that Biden won't circumvent them.
sentences.zh: 而共和党人也不相信拜登不会绕过他们。

sentences.en: So it's almost self-reinforcing.
sentences.zh: 所以这几乎是自我强化的。

sentences.en: That lack of trust reflects a divided electorate, an angry electorate, people turning against each other in this country.
sentences.zh: 这种缺乏信任反映了一个分裂的选民群体，一个愤怒的选民群体，在这个国家里人们彼此对立。

sentences.en: And I think it has made even routine things like raising a debt limit not at all routine.
sentences.zh: 我认为这使得即使是像提高债务上限这样的常规事情也变得一点都不常规了。

sentences.en: And the president has sort of had enough of this.
sentences.zh: 总统对此有点受够了。

sentences.en: He led the negotiations in 2011 to resolve the debt limit standoff.
sentences.zh: 他在2011年领导了谈判以解决债务上限僵局。

sentences.en: And this time he's just done with it.
sentences.zh: 而这一次他只是受够了。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to be negotiating over the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 他不想就债务上限进行谈判。

sentences.en: He does not see it as appropriate.
sentences.zh: 他不认为这是合适的。

sentences.en: He sees it as hostage taking.
sentences.zh: 他认为这是劫持人质。

sentences.en: And so for all those reasons, this does not feel the same as those previous fights to me.
sentences.zh: 所以出于所有这些原因，这对我来说感觉不像以前的那些争斗。

sentences.en: And that raises the possibility that it could end differently.
sentences.zh: 这增加了它可能以不同方式结束的可能性。

sentences.en: Jim, thank you.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: President Biden, Speaker McCarthy and other congressional leaders were scheduled to meet at the White House again this afternoon to continue their negotiations over the debt limit.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统、麦卡锡议长和其他国会领导人原定于今天下午再次在白宫会面，继续就债务上限进行谈判。

sentences.en: But on Thursday, the White House announced that that meeting had been postponed.
sentences.zh: 但周四，白宫宣布该会议已被推迟。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wynna Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜·刘。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢试着捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作“拼字蜜蜂”和“字母盒”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的。

sentences.en: Like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游玩。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Thursday, Manhattan prosecutors said that they would bring criminal charges against Daniel Penny,
sentences.zh: 周四，曼哈顿检察官表示，他们将对丹尼尔·彭尼提起刑事指控，

sentences.en: the 24-year-old Marine veteran who choked and killed a homeless man on the subway.
sentences.zh: 这名24岁的海军陆战队退伍军人在地铁上勒死了一名无家可归的男子。

sentences.en: The district attorney's office said it would charge Penny with second-degree manslaughter in the killing of Jordan Neely on an F-train on May 1St.
sentences.zh: 地区检察官办公室表示，将以二级过失杀人罪起诉彭尼，指控他在5月1日于F线地铁上杀害了乔丹·尼利。

sentences.en: Penny is expected to appear in Manhattan criminal court on Friday.
sentences.zh: 预计彭尼将于周五在曼哈顿刑事法庭出庭。

sentences.en: And the Food and Drug Administration announced that it has formally ended a long-standing policy of not accepting blood donations from gay and bisexual men.
sentences.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局宣布，已正式结束一项长期以来禁止男同性恋和双性恋男性献血的政策。

sentences.en: Instead, the agency is finalizing new guidance that will require all blood donors to fill out a questionnaire about their recent sexual activity.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，该机构正在敲定一项新指南，要求所有献血者填写一份关于近期性活动的问卷。

sentences.en: The change effectively ends a federal policy that had long been considered discriminatory.
sentences.zh: 这一改变实际上终结了一项长期以来被认为具有歧视性的联邦政策。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko and Alex Stern.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗布·齐普科和亚历克斯·斯特恩制作。

sentences.zh: 由安妮塔·巴达乔剪辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和罗文·内米斯托的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansvork of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯沃克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。
